answer: DeepWalk can exploit edge weights by turning them into transition probabilities in its random walks, so stronger connections are sampled more often and the learned embeddings reflect the network’s real interaction strengths. On a language network, where weighted links often encode meaningful co-occurrence or association strength, this lets DeepWalk preserve both local and higher-order structure more faithfully. LINE, by contrast, is primarily designed around first- and second-order proximity objectives and does not use the same random-walk-based higher-order context in a way that can leverage weighted paths as effectively. As a result, DeepWalk can capture richer neighborhood semantics from the weighted graph, which can translate into a much larger performance gain on that dataset.
